    Nobel Prize

          The Nobel Prize, established by Alfred Nobel, is a set of prestigious international
          awards that recognize contributions benefiting humankind.

          The prizes were funded by Alfred Nobel’s 1895 will, and the first awards were
           presented in 1901.

     Pulitzer Prize

          The Pulitzer Prizes were established through Joseph Pulitzer’s 1904 will and have
          been awarded since 1917.

          Joseph Pulitzer was a Hungarian-born American newspaper publisher who founded
            the prizes.

          The Pulitzer Prizes are administered by Columbia University.

          The Pulitzer Prizes are considered the most prestigious awards in the United States
              for journalism, literature, and music.

    Oscars

          The Oscars, officially known as the Academy Awards, are prestigious awards
           presented annually by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (AMPAS) to
           honor excellence in cinematic achievements.

           Since 2002, Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles, California, USA has been the fixed venue
            of these awards.

          The awards are given in 20+ categories. Among them, the “big five” awards are Best
             Picture, Best Director, Best Actor in a Leading Role, Best Actress in a Leading Role,
          and Best Screenplay (divided into Original and Adapted).

          The Academy Award for Best International Feature Film is an important category
          because full-length non-English films are recognized only under this category.
